onNoTags.description:
OnNoTags decides what happens when the selected scenarios have no tags:
"fallback" (start all enabled services, default) or "error".

CommandHookWhole.description: CommandHook runs a command before or after one of axx's commands, from the directory of axx.yaml.

after.description:
After names the axx command it runs after, whether that command
succeeded or failed: AXX_COMMAND_FAILED is true or false. When it fails,
a command that succeeded fails.

before.description:
Before names the axx command it runs before, by its words after axx:
fixtures generate. When it fails, that command does not run.

command.description:
Command is what it runs: a string (split like a shell word list,
without a shell) or an argv list. Set shell: true to run it through the
shell.

shell.description: Shell runs command through /bin/sh -c (cmd /C on Windows).

oneOf.description: command line, split into words without a shell unless shell: true

Docs.description: Docs is where the project's people read axx's documentation: the port `axx docs serve` serves it on, and the copy the links axx prints lead to (an organization's own, or `axx docs serve`'s), for a network that cannot reach the public site.

port.description:
Port is the port `axx docs serve` serves the docs on, on 127.0.0.1: 7357
unless set. Its --port flag wins.

url.description:
URL is the address of the docs site the links axx prints lead to (the
docs line of an error, the help's last line): an organization's copy,
like https://axx-docs.example.com, or http://127.0.0.1:7357 for `axx docs
serve`. The AXX_DOCS_URL environment variable wins; without either, they
lead to https://axx.nimbusxr.us.

FixtureConformanceWhole.description: FixtureConformance validates matched files against a schema.

filePatterns.description: FilePatterns are globs (relative to baseDir) of the files to validate.

name.description: Name is shown in check output.

schemaRef.description:
SchemaRef is the schema, relative to baseDir (unlike factory.schema,
which is relative to the factory file).

schemaType.description:
SchemaType is the family whose oracle validates the files: avro,
json, yaml, xml, protobuf or dataset.

FixtureLint.description: FixtureLint configures the generated lint rules.

emit.description:
Emit writes one cross-file-unique lint rule per declared identity.
Default: true.

output.description:
Output is the generated rules file, relative to baseDir. Default:
axx-lint.generated.yaml. Wire it in with lint.include.

ignored.description:
Ignored makes outputs gitignored derivations instead of committed
files: the tool maintains exact .gitignore entries and `axx fixtures
generate` materializes them. Default: false.

Fixtures.description: Fixtures configures `axx fixtures`, the fixture factory: *.factory.yaml, *.fixture.yaml and *.prototype.yaml sources expanded into schema-governed fixture files, with the ownership manifest, drift and conformance checks.

baseDir.description:
BaseDir is the resource root every fixtures path resolves against,
relative to axx.yaml. Default: the directory of axx.yaml.

conformance.description:
Conformance rules validate files no factory manages through a
family's schema oracle.

factories.description:
Factories are globs (relative to baseDir) locating factory specs.
Default: ["**.factory.yaml"].

lint.description: Lint configures the lint rules generated from identity declarations.

output.description:
Output holds module-wide output defaults; factories override them
with factory.output.

sources.description:
Sources are additional roots, relative to baseDir ("../" reaches
outside it), walked for factory, prototype and fixture sources exactly
like baseDir, so fixtures can sit next to generated files that live
elsewhere (a compose-mounted WireMock directory, say). Roots must
exist and be disjoint from baseDir and each other.

Fmt.description: Fmt is how `axx fmt`, and editors through axx lsp, lay out the project's feature files.

indent.description: Indent is the spaces of one level of indentation: 2 (the default) or 4.

Hooks.description: Hooks run the project's own commands around axx's, by what they run around.

commands.description:
Commands run before or after axx's commands, like `axx fixtures
generate`: a schema to write before fixtures are made from it, a report
to send after a run.

Lint.description: Lint configures `axx lint`: test-data isolation rules.

config.description: Config holds the settings shared by every rule.

include.description:
Include lists rule files merged into this section (for example the
axx-lint.generated.yaml written by `axx fixtures generate`), resolved
relative to the including file. Included files contribute rules and
further includes only; they must not have a config block.

rules.description: Rules are the isolation rules, run in order (included rules follow).

LintConfig.description: LintConfig holds the settings shared by every lint rule.

baseDir.description:
BaseDir is the directory file patterns are resolved against, relative
to axx.yaml. Default: the directory of axx.yaml.

maxFileSize.description:
MaxFileSize skips files larger than this many bytes, with a warning.
Default: 5242880 (5 MB).

maxReportedLocations.description:
MaxReportedLocations is how many locations the human output lists per
duplicate value before truncating. Default: 5. Machine formats list all.

maxReportedValues.description:
MaxReportedValues is how many duplicate values the human output lists
per rule before truncating. Default: 3. Machine formats list all.

mode.description:
Mode is "error" (violations make `axx lint` exit 3, default) or "warn"
(violations are reported but do not fail, a scenario's second When or Then
included).

LintRuleWhole.description: LintRule is one test-data isolation rule.

description.description: Description says why the values must be unique; shown with violations.

excludePatterns.description:
ExcludePatterns are glob patterns removing files from the match set,
matched against the whole path relative to baseDir; ** crosses
directories, e.g. "**.fixture.yaml".

filePatterns.description:
FilePatterns are glob patterns (Java glob syntax: *, **, ?, [abc],
{a,b}) selecting the files to scan, relative to baseDir. The part
before the first wildcard is a directory (it may start with ../); the
rest is matched against the end of each file path below it, so
"seeds/*.yaml" also finds YAML files in subdirectories of seeds. A
pattern that ends in "/" matches folders, and all the files below
each folder it matches count as one file: a scenario whose data spans
several files keeps them in a folder of its own ("seeds/*/"), whose
files may share values that no other file may.

ignoreValues.description: IgnoreValues are values never reported (intentionally shared constants).

jsonPath.description:
JSONPath selects the values of a jsonpath rule, e.g. "order.id",
"payments[*].id" or "$.items[0].sku" (exact field paths with array
indexes or [*]); other JSONPath expressions ("$..id", filters) are
evaluated like Jayway JsonPath. Only scalar values count. A seed's rows
read alike in YAML, flat XML (<dataset>) and CSV: "$['public.closures'][*]['id']";
in other XML, attributes are "@name" fields ("line[*].@sku") and an
element with only text is a value.

mode.description: Mode overrides config.mode for this rule: "error" or "warn".

name.description: Name identifies the rule in reports.

regex.description:
Regex is a Java regular expression, applied in MULTILINE mode (^ and $
match at line boundaries). Each match contributes the text of its
first participating capture group.

type.description:
Type is "regex" (default: extract values with regex) or "jsonpath"
(read each file, by its extension, as JSON, YAML, XML or CSV, and
extract the values at jsonPath).

validation.description:
Validation is "global-unique" (default: a value may occur once),
"file-unique" (no repeats within a file; files may share values) or
"cross-file-unique" (repeats within one file are fine; no two files
may share a value). A folder a folder pattern matches counts as one
file.

OpenAPI.description: OpenAPI holds default validation levels, keyed by validation message key (e.g.

coverage.description:
Coverage measures the coverage of the services that have a coverage
section, as the run exercises them, with the packs of their
runtimes. Same as axx run --coverage.

exclusive.description: Exclusive lists tags whose scenarios run alone, after the parallel phase.

exclusiveUses.description:
ExclusiveUses runs alone, after the parallel phase, the scenarios that use
a step of one of these packs, or one of these steps: its ID, or the start
of its ID, like [faults, sql.trigger]. A way to have them run alone with no
tags, which nothing turns on for you.

paths.description: Paths are feature files or directories. Default: ["features"].

slowdown.description:
Slowdown pauses after each action of a watched run (a click, a tap, a
typed field), so a person can follow it, e.g. "500ms". Same as
axx run --slowdown.

tags.description:
Tags is a default tag expression, e.g. "not @wip". It narrows every run,
the files and directories named on the command line included; a scenario
picked by its line (features/x.feature:14) runs whatever its tags.

uses.description:
Uses keeps the scenarios that use a step of one of these packs, like
[mobile-ios] for the scenarios that drive an iOS app: a profile per
platform, with no tags. Like tags, it narrows every run but a scenario
picked by its line.

watch.description:
Watch shows what the scenarios do, as they do it: the packs that can
show it on screen do (browsers and devices in their windows). Same as
axx run --watch.

workers.description:
Workers is the number of scenarios run in parallel: a number or "auto"
(number of CPUs). Default: auto.

additionalProperties.description: Service is an application or piece of infrastructure managed by axx.

tags.description: Tags start the service for the scenarios that have one of them.

uses.description:
Uses starts the service for the scenarios that use a step of one of these
packs, like [mobile-android]: no tag needed.

cleanup.description: Cleanup runs after the service stops, even if it crashed.

oneOf.description: command line, split into words without a shell unless shell: true

command.description:
Command starts the service: a string (split like a shell word list, without
a shell) or an argv list. Set shell: true to run it through the shell.
It can tell axx properties, like the ports Docker gave its containers:
lines name=value in the file AXX_PROPERTIES names, which scenarios,
readiness checks and the services that depend on it read as
${sys:name}. Its ${…} references, and those of env and cleanup, are
filled in as the service starts, with what the services it depends on
told.

oneOf.description: command line, split into words without a shell unless shell: true

coverage.description:
Coverage is how the service runs when a run measures its coverage
(axx run --coverage): the pack of its runtime measures it.

command.description:
Command replaces command when the run measures the service, as
debug.command does: a build for coverage (go build -cover), or the
command under coverage.py.

oneOf.description: command line, split into words without a shell unless shell: true

env.description:
Env are variables the service gets beside env when the run measures
it.

runtime.description:
Runtime is what measures it: a runtime a coverage pack adds, like jvm
(coverage-jvm), go, python or node, or report, for a service that
writes lcov or Cobertura into its folder itself.

command.description: Command replaces the normal command in debug mode.

oneOf.description: command line, split into words without a shell unless shell: true

mode.description:
Mode is "ide-listens" (the IDE listens and the service connects, e.g. JDWP
server=n; default for java) or "app-listens" (delve, --inspect, debugpy).

onUnavailable.description:
OnUnavailable decides what happens when the debugger is not listening:
fail, fallback (run the normal command) or retry (default).

dependsOn.description:
DependsOn names services that must be ready first: what they tell axx
fills in this one's command, env and cleanup.

dir.description: Dir is the working directory, relative to axx.yaml.

env.description: Env are variables the command gets, beside axx's own environment.

exec.description: Exec is a command that must exit 0.

oneOf.description: command line, split into words without a shell unless shell: true

log.description: Log is a regular expression matched against the service's output.

tcp.description: TCP is a host:port that must accept connections.

timeout.description: Timeout for the service to become ready. Default: 60s.

shell.description: Shell runs command and cleanup through /bin/sh -c (cmd /C on Windows).

grace.description: Grace period before the process group is killed. Default: 10s.

signal.description: Signal sent first: SIGTERM (default) or SIGINT.

Timeouts.description: Timeouts bound steps, scenarios and hooks.

description: An overlay of axx.yaml: a profile's file (axx.<name>.yaml, chosen with --profile or AXX_PROFILE) or axx.local.yaml. It says only what differs from axx.yaml. axx lays it over axx.yaml, mapping by mapping (a list replaces the list under it), and checks the result, so nothing is required here that axx.yaml says already.

active.description: Active starts only the applications needed by the selected scenarios.

axx.description:
Axx is the version of axx this project runs on, exactly. Whichever axx is
installed downloads that release once and hands over to it, so that everyone
and CI run the same one. `axx upgrade` moves it. Without it, a project runs
on the installed axx.

docs.description:
Docs configures where the project's people read axx's documentation:
`axx docs serve`'s port, and where the links axx prints lead.

fmt.description:
Fmt configures how `axx fmt`, and editors through axx lsp, lay out
feature files.

hooks.description:
Hooks run the project's own commands around axx's, by what they run
around.

lint.description:
Lint configures `axx lint`: test-data isolation rules that keep values
such as seed ids unique so scenarios can run in parallel.

openapi.description: OpenAPI holds default OpenAPI validation settings for REST services.

packs.description: Packs holds pack settings keyed by pack name.

profiles.description: Profiles are named overlays selected with --profile or AXX_PROFILE.

properties.description:
Properties back ${sys:name} references. `-D name=value` overrides them,
and they override what services write to the file AXX_PROPERTIES
names: a value you set always wins.

resources.description:
Resources are directories that relative resource paths in steps (seed
files, schemas, payloads) resolve against, in order, once the feature
file's own directory has not got the file. The directory of axx.yaml is
always searched last.

run.description: Run controls which features run and how.

services.description:
Services are the applications under test (and their infrastructure),
started before scenarios run and stopped afterwards, in declaration order.

version.description: Schema version of this file. Currently 1.

title: axx.<profile>.yaml
